From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Re:** Where the Seller's package departs from Buyer interests, and recommended pushback

## Overview

The Seller describes the package as "fair and balanced". It is not. Read together, the SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter do three things: (1) shrink the warranty protection to the point where it is close to illusory (low cap, short period, deductible basket, constructive-knowledge bar, blanket data room disclosure, fundamental warranties folded into the general regime); (2) push the four live diligence problems — Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and the DD-006 incident — past Completion and onto us; and (3) leave AUD ~4.0m+ of debt-like items (Riverlark AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k plus on-costs, Sandbar AUD 330k) outside the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics.

Notably, the Disclosure Letter itself is more candid than the Seller Update. Items 2–6 concede that the Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay assignment and bonus funding are *not* in place. We should use the Seller's own disclosures against the Seller's own negotiating positions.

Issues are ordered by materiality.

---

## A. Deal-structure issues (money and conditions)

### 1. Riverlark facility — release "following Completion" (Cl 2 / 7; DL item 3)
**Departure:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free, yet the Seller proposes that a ~AUD 3.2m facility stays in place at Completion with a release to follow. The DL confirms it is unrepaid and no discharge is in the data room. DD-003 has a change-of-control clause (8.1), so Completion without consent/repayment is likely an event of default on day one of our ownership. Security over Company assets (and probably over the shares) would survive.
**Pushback:**
- Repayment at Completion from the funds flow, with the amount deducted from the price (or paid directly to Riverlark on the Seller's behalf).
- Completion deliverables: signed payout letter, deed of release, release of any Seller/director guarantees, executed PPSR discharge (and release of any share mortgage) — all delivered *at* Completion, not after.
- If the Seller insists on post-Completion mechanics, the AUD 3.2m is withheld/escrowed until discharge is registered. No other outcome is acceptable.

### 2. Bluefen consent — ~30% of revenue (Cl 3 / 6.3; DL item 2)
**Departure:** "Reasonable endeavours" plus "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is weak on two fronts. First, DL item 2 says the consent is not obtained and the clause 11.3 *conditions* are unsatisfied — a bare written consent with unsatisfied conditions should not satisfy the CP. Second, "reasonable endeavours" is the lowest endeavours standard; the Seller controls the relationship pre-Completion.
**Pushback:**
- Condition Precedent: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, *or* consent with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen, on terms not adverse to the Company, in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably).
- "All reasonable endeavours" / "best endeavours", Buyer right to participate in communications with Bluefen, Seller not to agree to any concession (price, term, exclusivity) without our approval.
- CP for the Buyer's sole benefit and waivable only by us; long-stop date; termination right.
- Express warranty that no Bluefen notice of termination, non-renewal or dispute has been given or threatened; price adjustment or escrow if the consent is granted with commercial conditions that cost the Company money.

### 3. Completion bonuses — AUD 420,000 excluded from funds flow (DD-005; DL item 5)
**Departure:** "A matter for the Seller" is only true if the Seller actually funds them. They are Company obligations triggered by Completion, paid through Company payroll, and not itemised in the funds flow. DL item 5 admits on-costs (superannuation ~12%, NSW payroll tax ~5.45%) are not addressed. The continued-employment condition means some will fall due *after* Completion — i.e., on our watch and out of our cash.
**Pushback:**
- Treat bonuses plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, PAYG remittance, any leave accruals) as Transaction Costs/Debt in the price mechanics — deducted from the price or paid by the Seller before Completion.
- Where payments fall due post-Completion, the amount (grossed up) is deducted from the price or held in escrow and released as paid.
- Confirm no other change-of-control payments, retention or equity awards exist (warranty + specific indemnity).

### 4. Ironquay IP — SOW3 materials not owned (Cl 11.1; DL item 4)
**Departure:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; AUD 180k is open and no assignment exists. Until then Ironquay, not the Company, owns the IP. The Seller's indemnity is limited to the AUD 180k payment — it does not cover the actual risk (defective title to IP, infringement claims, inability to use/licence the materials, cost of re-development, loss of customers).
**Pushback:**
- CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment to Ironquay *and* a confirmatory deed of assignment of all SOW3 (and ideally all SOW) IP to the Company, with moral-rights consents.
- Pay the AUD 180k out of the price if necessary (it is a pre-Completion liability).
- Specific indemnity widened to all Loss arising from the Company not holding full, unencumbered title to any Ironquay-developed IP — outside the de minimis/basket, with its own cap (at least 100% of price) and 6-year period.
- Robust IP ownership warranties (see F below). Ask the Seller what the SOW3 materials actually are — if they are core to the Paperbark product, this is potentially a go/no-go item.

### 5. DD-006 export incident — "not expected to be material" (Cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DL item 6)
**Departure:** A download link to ~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address is, on its face, a potential "eligible data breach" under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988). The Seller's own DL says access, scope and notification are *unknown* and the investigation is *preliminary*. The Seller cannot simultaneously say it is unknown and not material. Timing matters: the 30-day assessment window and any notification obligation may be running now. Civil penalties for serious/repeated interferences with privacy were sharply increased in 2022 and the regime has been further tightened since.
**Pushback:**
- Completion of the assessment (and any OAIC/individual notifications) before Completion, with the report provided to us; Buyer approval of the notification decision.
- Specific indemnity for all Loss from the incident (investigation, notification, regulator engagement, penalties, third-party and contractual claims, remediation), not subject to de minimis/basket/general cap/disclosure, with a 6-year period; consider a dedicated escrow.
- Privacy and data-security warranties; disclosure of the incident must *not* qualify the indemnity.
- Check whether Bluefen or other customer data is in the export — this interacts with Issue 2.

### 6. Sandbar supplier renewals — 3 × AUD 110,000 (DL item 8)
**Departure:** "Ordinary-course operating costs" is asserted, not evidenced. The DL expressly declines to say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Three identical AUD 110k items are curiously sized — check whether the split is designed to sit below any materiality threshold in the SPA or in the Seller's contracting authority limits.
**Pushback:**
- Diligence follow-up: commitment dates, terms, termination rights, whether services are needed post-Completion.
- If committed pre-Completion for post-Completion periods or outside budget, treat as Debt-like or run through the working-capital adjustment; conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for commitments > AUD [50k] between signing and Completion.
- Warranty that no supplier commitments outside the ordinary course have been entered into.

---

## B. Warranty protection regime

### 7. General cap — 20% / AUD 4.8m (Cl 12.1)
**Departure:** Low for a private mid-market Australian deal of this size without W&I insurance, and especially low given the open items above. Our starting point should be 100%; a landing zone of 40–50% is defensible if the specific indemnities are carved out and separately capped. If the Seller will not move, W&I insurance (with the Seller funding part of the premium) is the alternative.

### 8. Fundamental and title warranties folded into general regime
**Departure:** This is the most dangerous single proposal. Title, capacity and authority warranties are universally outside the general cap and time limits. If the shares are not validly owned by Harbourglass, a 20% cap and 18-month window is absurd — we would have paid AUD 24m for nothing and be able to recover AUD 4.8m. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
**Pushback:** Title/capacity/authority warranties: cap at 100% of price (or uncapped), 6–7 year limitation (or statutory), no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure or knowledge qualifiers.

### 9. Thresholds — AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k deductible basket (Cl 12.2)
**Departure:** The basket is a *deductible* (only the excess is recoverable). Combined with the de minimis, the Seller is effectively asking for a free AUD 250k plus every claim under AUD 25k.
**Pushback:** Tipping basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded); de minimis ~AUD 10–15k; related claims arising from the same facts aggregated for both thresholds; thresholds not to apply to Fundamental Warranties, Tax, specific indemnities, leakage or Completion-obligation breaches.

### 10. Time limits — 18 months, and "all limitations apply to all Claims" (Cl 12.3 / 13)
**Departure:** 18 months may not cover one full audit cycle post-Completion. More importantly, the default rule proposed — every limitation applies to every Claim unless the SPA says otherwise — reverses the normal drafting and will catch indemnity claims, covenant breaches and Completion obligations by accident (or design).
**Pushback:** General warranties 24 months (minimum 18 months only if cap/basket improve); Tax 7 years; Fundamental and IP 6–7 years; specific indemnities 6 years. Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. Claims notified in time survive if proceedings commence within 9–12 months.

### 11. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance on "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Departure:** Drafted this broadly, these would cap or exclude claims for fraud, wilful concealment, breach of the specific indemnities, leakage, restraints, and Completion obligations. Exclusion of liability for fraud is unenforceable; exclusion of liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contracted out of directly, and a non-reliance clause of this width will be read against the Seller — but we should not rely on litigation to fix bad drafting.
**Pushback:** Express carve-outs for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct/concealment; specific indemnities; tax indemnity; leakage; restraints; Completion obligations and post-Completion covenants. Non-reliance limited to statements *outside* the SPA, disclosure letter and specifically identified DD responses, and not applying to fraud or statutory claims.

### 12. Disclosure standard — general disclosure of the data room and public registers (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
**Departure:** Blanket disclosure of DD-002 to DD-012, the Accounts, statutory registers *and* "publicly searchable corporate records" means anything buried in any document, or findable on any register, defeats a warranty claim. Combined with Issue 13, this removes virtually all warranty value.
**Pushback:**
- "Fairly disclosed" standard: disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
- Data room disclosure only against the specific warranty it fairly qualifies, by reference to a frozen, indexed USB/record of the data room as at a stated date and time.
- Public register disclosure limited to specific ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches, named and dated, with results annexed.
- Accounts disclosed only against the Accounts warranties.
- Note the DL cut-off (22 Sept 2026) is six weeks stale — require a bring-down disclosure letter at Completion with Buyer rights (termination/price adjustment) for material new disclosures, and no right to disclose against the specific indemnities or Fundamental Warranties.
- Why DD-002 to DD-012 — where is DD-001? Confirm whether it exists and why it is excluded.

### 13. Buyer knowledge — including matters "discoverable" from data room or public records (Cl 8.3)
**Departure:** A constructive-knowledge bar. Together with Issue 12 it is double-dipping: the Seller gets disclosure protection *and* a knowledge bar for anything we might have found. This is a clause to strike, not amend.
**Pushback:** Delete. Fall-back: actual knowledge of up to three named Buyer deal-team individuals, limited to matters where they actually knew both the facts and that they constituted a warranty breach; no imputation from advisers; no "discoverable"; no application to Fundamental Warranties, Tax or specific indemnities. (If the Seller wants anti-sandbagging, insist on a pro-sandbagging clause as the alternative.)

---

## C. Other items

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Departure:** Not acceptable. Australian practice is a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or capped at 100%, 7 years), tax warranties and conduct-of-tax-claims provisions. IP warranties need their own longer period and, given Ironquay, specific ownership/chain-of-title content (all contractor and employee IP assigned, no open-source contamination of proprietary code, no infringement claims).

### 15. Title — share register at DD-012 only (DL item 10)
**Departure:** The register is prima facie but not conclusive evidence. DL item 10 pointedly says we have not verified. Do so: ASIC company search and historical extract; share certificates; PPSR search against the Seller and the Company (likely a share mortgage to Riverlark — ties to Issue 1); any options, ESOP, convertible notes or shareholder agreements (the bonus scheme suggests employee incentives exist — confirm none are equity-settled); constitution pre-emption rights. Then uncapped title warranty (Issue 8).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller's reading (notification only; no consent on a share sale) may be right, but we should read the clauses ourselves: "assignment" restrictions often include change-of-control wording. Require the lease notification to be given pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion, and a warranty that no counterparty consent is required for the transaction other than those listed in the SPA.

### 17. Disclosure Letter 1.4 and item 11
Standard non-admission language; acceptable, but ensure the SPA provides that disclosure does not qualify any specific indemnity, Fundamental Warranty or the price mechanics.

---

## Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Item | Position to take |
|---|------|------------------|
| 1 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Repay at Completion from funds flow; release, guarantee release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables; otherwise withhold the amount |
| 2 | Bluefen consent | Hard CP: unconditional consent (or 11.3 conditions satisfied), Buyer-approved form, all reasonable endeavours, Buyer-only waiver, long-stop |
| 3 | Fundamental/title warranties | Out of general regime: 100% cap, 6–7 years, no thresholds, no disclosure/knowledge qualifier |
| 4 | Cl 8.3 knowledge bar | Delete; fall-back actual knowledge of named individuals, no "discoverable" |
| 5 | Disclosure standard | "Fairly disclosed", specific-to-warranty, frozen data room, named searches only; bring-down DL with Buyer rights |
| 6 | Ironquay IP | Payment + confirmatory assignment as CP; broad IP-title indemnity, separate cap and period |
| 7 | DD-006 incident | Complete assessment/notification pre-Completion; uncapped/separately capped specific indemnity; escrow |
| 8 | Bonuses AUD 420k + on-costs | Treat as Transaction Costs/Debt; deduct or escrow; warranty/indemnity on other change-of-control payments |
| 9 | Cap / thresholds / time | Open at 100% cap, land 40–50% (or W&I); tipping basket, lower de minimis; 24 months general, 7 years tax |
| 10 | Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 | Carve out fraud, indemnities, tax, leakage, restraints, Completion obligations; narrow non-reliance |
| 11 | Tax/IP | Standalone tax indemnity and tax warranties; expanded IP warranties |
| 12 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Diligence; treat as Debt-like/working capital if committed outside ordinary course; interim-period consent covenant |
| 13 | Title verification; lease/Mossvale | Run ASIC/PPSR searches, check for equity awards; verify consent clauses; pre-Completion notices |

**Overall posture:** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter concedes that none of the four critical items is resolved. Our response should make clear that the price was agreed on a debt-free/cash-free basis for a business with its key contract, its IP and a clean balance sheet intact — and that each unresolved item is either fixed before Completion, deducted from the price, or backed by a specific indemnity and escrow. Consider a general retention (e.g. 10% for 18–24 months) given the thinness of the Seller's covenant if Harbourglass is a special-purpose holding entity; confirm its financial standing or seek a parent/shareholder guarantee.

*Points of Australian law above (NDB scheme, ACL s18, Corporations Act s176, payroll tax/super rates) should be confirmed by the deal's Australian counsel before being put to the Seller.*

## B. Warranty protection regime

### 7. General cap — 20% / AUD 4.8m (Cl 12.1)
**Departure:** Low for a private mid-market Australian deal of this size without W&I insurance, and especially low given the open items above. Our starting point should be 100%; a landing zone of 40–50% is defensible if the specific indemnities are carved out and separately capped. If the Seller will not move, W&I insurance (with the Seller funding part of the premium) is the alternative.

### 8. Fundamental and title warranties folded into general regime
**Departure:** This is the most dangerous single proposal. Title, capacity and authority warranties are universally outside the general cap and time limits. If the shares are not validly owned by Harbourglass, a 20% cap and 18-month window is absurd — we would have paid AUD 24m for nothing and be able to recover AUD 4.8m. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
**Pushback:** Title/capacity/authority warranties: cap at 100% of price (or uncapped), 6–7 year limitation (or statutory), no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure or knowledge qualifiers.

### 9. Thresholds — AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k deductible basket (Cl 12.2)
**Departure:** The basket is a *deductible* (only the excess is recoverable). Combined with the de minimis, the Seller is effectively asking for a free AUD 250k plus every claim under AUD 25k.
**Pushback:** Tipping basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded); de minimis ~AUD 10–15k; related claims arising from the same facts aggregated for both thresholds; thresholds not to apply to Fundamental Warranties, Tax, specific indemnities, leakage or Completion-obligation breaches.

### 10. Time limits — 18 months, and "all limitations apply to all Claims" (Cl 12.3 / 13)
**Departure:** 18 months may not cover one full audit cycle post-Completion. More importantly, the default rule proposed — every limitation applies to every Claim unless the SPA says otherwise — reverses the normal drafting and will catch indemnity claims, covenant breaches and Completion obligations by accident (or design).
**Pushback:** General warranties 24 months (minimum 18 months only if cap/basket improve); Tax 7 years; Fundamental and IP 6–7 years; specific indemnities 6 years. Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. Claims notified in time survive if proceedings commence within 9–12 months.

### 11. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance on "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
**Departure:** Drafted this broadly, these would cap or exclude claims for fraud, wilful concealment, breach of the specific indemnities, leakage, restraints, and Completion obligations. Exclusion of liability for fraud is unenforceable; exclusion of liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law cannot be contracted out of directly, and a non-reliance clause of this width will be read against the Seller — but we should not rely on litigation to fix bad drafting.
**Pushback:** Express carve-outs for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct/concealment; specific indemnities; tax indemnity; leakage; restraints; Completion obligations and post-Completion covenants. Non-reliance limited to statements *outside* the SPA, disclosure letter and specifically identified DD responses, and not applying to fraud or statutory claims.

### 12. Disclosure standard — general disclosure of the data room and public registers (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2)
**Departure:** Blanket disclosure of DD-002 to DD-012, the Accounts, statutory registers *and* "publicly searchable corporate records" means anything buried in any document, or findable on any register, defeats a warranty claim. Combined with Issue 13, this removes virtually all warranty value.
**Pushback:**
- "Fairly disclosed" standard: disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and financial effect of the matter.
- Data room disclosure only against the specific warranty it fairly qualifies, by reference to a frozen, indexed USB/record of the data room as at a stated date and time.
- Public register disclosure limited to specific ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches, named and dated, with results annexed.
- Accounts disclosed only against the Accounts warranties.
- Note the DL cut-off (22 Sept 2026) is six weeks stale — require a bring-down disclosure letter at Completion with Buyer rights (termination/price adjustment) for material new disclosures, and no right to disclose against the specific indemnities or Fundamental Warranties.
- Why DD-002 to DD-012 — where is DD-001? Confirm whether it exists and why it is excluded.

### 13. Buyer knowledge — including matters "discoverable" from data room or public records (Cl 8.3)
**Departure:** A constructive-knowledge bar. Together with Issue 12 it is double-dipping: the Seller gets disclosure protection *and* a knowledge bar for anything we might have found. This is a clause to strike, not amend.
**Pushback:** Delete. Fall-back: actual knowledge of up to three named Buyer deal-team individuals, limited to matters where they actually knew both the facts and that they constituted a warranty breach; no imputation from advisers; no "discoverable"; no application to Fundamental Warranties, Tax or specific indemnities. (If the Seller wants anti-sandbagging, insist on a pro-sandbagging clause as the alternative.)

## C. Other items

### 14. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
**Departure:** Not acceptable. Australian practice is a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, uncapped or capped at 100%, 7 years), tax warranties and conduct-of-tax-claims provisions. IP warranties need their own longer period and, given Ironquay, specific ownership/chain-of-title content (all contractor and employee IP assigned, no open-source contamination of proprietary code, no infringement claims).

### 15. Title — share register at DD-012 only (DL item 10)
**Departure:** The register is prima facie but not conclusive evidence. DL item 10 pointedly says we have not verified. Do so: ASIC company search and historical extract; share certificates; PPSR search against the Seller and the Company (likely a share mortgage to Riverlark — ties to Issue 1); any options, ESOP, convertible notes or shareholder agreements (the bonus scheme suggests employee incentives exist — confirm none are equity-settled); constitution pre-emption rights. Then uncapped title warranty (Issue 8).

### 16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Seller's reading (notification only; no consent on a share sale) may be right, but we should read the clauses ourselves: "assignment" restrictions often include change-of-control wording. Require the lease notification to be given pre-Completion with evidence delivered at Completion, and a warranty that no counterparty consent is required for the transaction other than those listed in the SPA.

### 17. Disclosure Letter 1.4 and item 11
Standard non-admission language; acceptable, but ensure the SPA provides that disclosure does not qualify any specific indemnity, Fundamental Warranty or the price mechanics.
